title: Shutdown leaves nothing running on either platform
statement: After Pi exits, after an interrupt, or after one Ctrl+C at the keyboard in an interactive Kiln session, both process trees are stopped within their grace periods, the port is free, and only files created by that invocation were removed. Seven things are observed and recorded SEPARATELY, because they fail separately and because any one of them standing for the others is how a shutdown claim becomes untestable. An observation that was not made is recorded as unmade and the shutdown is reported partial; it is never treated as one that passed. (1) Which of the three triggers ended the run — Pi exiting on its own, a signal, or the keyboard stop — each recorded where it was observed rather than supplied beside it, so the record cannot contradict itself. A signal is recorded where it was handled and never inferred from the processes having gone. The keyboard stop exists because an interactive Pi reads Ctrl+C as a key, so no signal occurs: Kiln's Pi extension consumes the key in the editor and in dialogs and writes a per-run notice before asking Pi to stop, and the stop is recorded as `keyboard` when the supervisor sees that notice, including when Pi's exit is observed first; it never records a signal that did not occur. A run ended by Pi exiting on its own records neither a signal nor a keyboard stop. (2) For each tree independently, either that it had already exited or that a stop was requested of it: a tree that was already gone is recorded as such and is not asked, and a supervisor that asks one tree and not the other looks identical to a correct one on every run where the unasked tree exits anyway. (3) That each tree's exit was independently observed, so one going never stands in for the other. (4) That where a graceful stop did not complete, escalation was bounded and its outcome observed — reported as unobserved rather than assumed when the process still did not go. (5) That the port accepts a fresh exclusive bind afterwards, observed by rebinding rather than derived from any process record: an exit code says the leader is gone and says nothing about a worker still listening. (6) That only runtime files this invocation created were removed, proved by a file it did not create still being present afterwards, not merely by its own being gone. (7) That the results are recorded independently for Windows and for the supported POSIX platform through CI, rather than one platform's pass standing for both, and that each platform's observation includes a KNOWN DESCENDANT of each tree rather than only the leader's exit code. The platforms differ in the only mechanism that matters here: a graceful signal is unavailable on Windows, and on POSIX a process group can be targeted only for a child spawned as a group leader — which the foreground agent cannot be, since a detached process cannot read the terminal, so its descendants must be enumerated and signalled individually. A descendant enumeration that fails is recorded as unmade, because an empty list would claim a tree with no children. Two bounds are stated separately, because they cover different work and are paid at different times. THE WINDOWS LAUNCH PREFLIGHT: before either child is started, the production process-table reader has up to 10,000 ms to return a table containing this supervisor's own pid and creation time. A read that times out, fails, or cannot show that identity refuses the launch, and neither Pi nor the launcher is spawned. This is a launch prerequisite, bounded on its own; its duration is never counted against the shutdown budget. POSIX does not run this Windows-specific preflight. THE SHUTDOWN: from the trigger — Pi exiting, an interrupt arriving, or the keyboard stop's notice being seen, without waiting for Pi to exit — the whole teardown has one 8,000 ms deadline, and every operation draws its allowance from it: the descendant tracker joins, each tree's grace and hard waits, every identity read, every signal or `taskkill`, the launcher's control channel, the removal of this invocation's owned files, and the port probe. An operation whose minimum allowance the deadline cannot cover is not started, is named in the record's `unfinished` list with its reason, and makes the result incomplete. A shutdown is complete only when all six hold: both trees were observed stopped; the port accepts a fresh exclusive bind; the removal of owned files succeeded; every required observation was made, so `notObserved` is empty; `unfinished` is empty; and `withinBudget` is true. A teardown that ran past its deadline is not complete, whatever else it managed.
notes: ⚠️ Reopened 2026-09-15 on R18 and R19; settled 2026-09-16. EVD-0088 stands unchanged as the historical record of commit 36df281. R18 was a real overrun and a criterion/evidence mismatch: run 34910936533 recorded spentMs 8092 against an 8,000 ms budget with withinBudget false, while the evidence test passed it against an unstated 9,500 ms ceiling, the budget plus six 250 ms phase floors. Identity reads and termination spawns ran outside every scaled wait, so neither the budget nor that ceiling bounded them. Both are closed: one deadline now covers every operation, that ceiling is deleted, and a completed result requires withinBudget. R19 is closed by a per-operation timeline that records when each tree was observed stopped. The 8,000 ms budget is unchanged; what changed is that it is enforced rather than described. F119, intermittent Windows WMI latency, is MITIGATED, NOT ELIMINATED: the provider's first use is now paid by the bounded launch preflight, measured at 3,142 ms and 3,057 ms on cold CI runners, after which every tracked query cost 370 to 830 ms. If a primed route times out again in CI, WMI is removed wholesale in favour of a WMI-free identity format, which is a deliberate change of identity precision and not a fallback. F119's successor is settled: F122 retired WMI after a primed timeout, and EVD-0111 records the WMI-free reader, the six complete Windows records under the enforced deadline, and F130 as instrumented but unexplained. ⚠️ FAIL 2026-09-24 on EVD-0146. After an interrupt on a loaded Windows runner (CI run 36074016941, job 107881093769), the launcher's identity read ran out of deadline. A launcher descendant was still running when the supervisor returned. The shutdown was correctly reported partial (launcher-descendants-unverified), but both trees were not stopped, and this criterion requires that they were. O1 (ca476de) fixed the natural-mode starvation and is verified for natural shutdown only. The pass is not restored until both open mechanisms are resolved: the live descendant after an interrupt, and the short-lived agent whose descendants the tracker never observes (F130, TSK-0058).
